reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended Locator reconnection leaves the shared endpoint stale, so new producers and consumers may select an unreachable address after mixed-family failover.
1 open issue - [Update the cached endpoint after locator reconnection](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-stream-dotnet-client/pull/495#discussion_r4587828120) · New
What changed in this PR This PR addresses #450 by making broker DNS resolution respect the configured endpoint’s address family, avoiding IPv6 selection when RabbitMQ is reachable only over IPv4. **Changes:** - Prefer DNS addresses matching the endpoint’s family, retaining first-address fallback behavior. - Preserve the endpoint that successfully connected for later routing. - Add broker-independent tests for IPv4, IPv6, unspecified-family, and missing-family selection. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `Tests/​UnitTests.cs` | Adds four address-selection regression tests. | | `RabbitMQ.Stream.Client/​StreamSystem.cs` | Retains the successfully connected endpoint in routing parameters. | | `RabbitMQ.Stream.Client/​RoutingClient.cs` | Applies address-family preference when resolving broker DNS. |
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body: After locator reconnection to a different address family, `_clientParameters.Endpoint` still holds the startup endpoint because `MayBeReconnectLocator` only replaces `_client`. New producers and consumers can therefore select an unreachable address for dual-stack broker names despite the locator reconnecting successfully. After a successful reconnect at lines 277–282, assign `_client.Parameters.Endpoint` to `_clientParameters.Endpoint` and add a mixed-family failover regression test.

Thanks @Gsantomaggio, the Broadcom/RabbitMQ CLA has been signed via Box Sign (completed). I'll also address the Copilot note about keeping `_clientParameters.Endpoint` in sync after a successful locator reconnect, with a regression test.

Pushed a follow-up for the Copilot note: after `MayBeReconnectLocator` connects, the connected endpoint is copied back to the shared `ClientParameters`, so producers and consumers created later resolve DNS with the address family of the endpoint that actually worked. Added a unit test for the sync helper. The CLA was signed via Box Sign earlier.

This follow-up was prepared with the help of an AI assistant (Claude) and submitted by the account holder.
